items.title: Locked timing and workspace defaults
items.statement: The LSP contract fixes didChange debounce at 100 ms, hover and completion timeouts at 5000 ms, workspace-symbol timeout at 10000 ms, hover delay at 300 ms, and workspaceFolders at no more than 10 roots that each have an open document.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The locked LSP defaults are didChangeDebounceMs 100, hoverTimeoutMs 5000, completionTimeoutMs 5000, workspaceSymbolTimeoutMs 10000, hoverDelayMs 300, and workspaceFolders capped at 10 roots with at least one open document.

items.title: Completion and inlay refresh triggers
items.statement: Completion prefers server-advertised trigger characters but retains typing and manual invocation; inlay hints refresh on document open and debounced change, while scroll-only refresh is excluded from MVP.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Trigger and refresh policy uses server-advertised completion trigger characters when available, keeps typing and manual invocation fallback, refreshes inlay hints on document open and debounced changes, does not require scroll-only refresh for MVP, and uses canonical hover delay and timeout values.

items.title: Deterministic workspace overflow evidence
items.statement: Only roots containing open documents enter workspaceFolders up to the cap, and behavior-affecting overflow exclusions must be deterministic and observable in logs and evidence.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: workspaceFolders includes only roots with at least one open document up to the configured cap, and deterministic overflow exclusions are visible in logs and evidence when they affect behavior.

items.title: Silent overflow is explicitly prohibited
items.statement: The negative constraint closes discretion to silently omit overflow roots whenever exclusion changes behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - Overflow workspace roots must not be silently hidden when exclusion affects behavior.

items.title: FileSafe owns LSP edit application safety
items.statement: workspace/applyEdit, rename, and code-action edits must traverse the FileSafe-backed mutation path and inherit its safety, approval, tool-policy, and blocked-state reporting rules, including for multi-file and destructive edits.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: workspace/applyEdit, rename, and code-action application use the same FileSafe-backed apply-edit path as other agent mutations, treating multi-file and destructive edits with the same safety, approval, tool-policy, and blocked-state reporting rules.

items.title: LSP mutation bypass is forbidden
items.statement: The core expressly forbids LSP from bypassing FileSafe, tool policy, or blocked-state reporting.

evidence.exact_quote: - LSP does not bypass FileSafe, tool policy, or blocked-state reporting.

items.title: Virtual-document decision remains closed
items.statement: Chat and code-block virtual documents must preserve the pre-existing stance and the PlanUnit declares that core runtime LSP behavior is not left implementation-defined after the implementer-decisions section.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Chat and code-block virtual documents keep the existing virtual-document stance and do not reopen that decision; no core runtime LSP behavior remains implementation-defined after the closed implementer decisions section.

items.title: Virtual-document stance is not restated in the core window
items.statement: The authoritative core invokes an existing virtual-document stance without stating its concrete lifecycle, synchronization, URI, edit, or consumer behavior in this window; those details cannot be recovered from the assigned evidence.
items.impact: A builder limited to this PlanUnit cannot implement or validate virtual-document behavior from the stated closure alone.
items.builder_discretion: Unknown in this window; the text denies discretion but does not reproduce the referenced stance.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Chat and code-block virtual documents keep the existing virtual-document stance and do not reopen that decision; no core runtime LSP behavior remains implementation-defined after the closed implementer decisions section.

items.title: Checklist is guidance, not executable work
items.statement: The phases 1-4 checklist is a non-executable acceptance guide and explicitly defers optional gate, evidence, subagent-bias, and enhancement work.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The implementation-ready checklist is a non-executable guide with acceptance criteria for prerequisites and phases 1-4, including diagnostics caps, Chat affordances, Problems links, and explicit deferral of optional gate, evidence, subagent-bias, and enhancement work.

items.title: Checklist contains direct GUI concerns
items.statement: The checklist is correctly classified as GUI-related because it covers user-visible editor, status, Problems, Settings, Chat, copy, evidence display, and interaction behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: gui_classification_reason: The unit defines user-visible editor, status, Problems, Settings, Chat, copy, evidence display, or interaction behavior.

items.title: Prerequisite implementation surfaces
items.statement: Prerequisites require a selected Rust stdio LSP client, Cargo integration, an OpenCode-aligned configuration schema, redb persistence, and debounce and timeout keys.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Prerequisites require choosing a Rust stdio-capable LSP client, adding it to Cargo.toml, defining OpenCode-aligned LSP config schema, storing it in redb, and adding debounce/timeout config keys.

items.title: Rust LSP client selection remains discretionary
items.statement: The prerequisite requires choosing a Rust stdio-capable client but does not lock the client or selection oracle within the authoritative core.
items.impact: Client-specific protocol behavior, maintenance burden, dependency graph, and compatibility can vary materially.
items.builder_discretion: Select any Rust stdio-capable client and infer evaluation criteria.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Prerequisites require choosing a Rust stdio-capable LSP client, adding it to Cargo.toml, defining OpenCode-aligned LSP config schema, storing it in redb, and adding debounce/timeout config keys.

items.title: Timeout outcomes and recovery are unspecified
items.statement: Timeout durations are locked, but the core does not define cancellation, user-visible reporting, retry, server restart, stale-result handling, or fallback behavior when a timeout fires.
items.impact: Implementations can diverge on observable failure state and recovery after hover, completion, or workspace-symbol timeouts.
items.builder_discretion: Choose timeout cancellation, reporting, retry, restart, and stale-result semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The locked LSP defaults are didChangeDebounceMs 100, hoverTimeoutMs 5000, completionTimeoutMs 5000, workspaceSymbolTimeoutMs 10000, hoverDelayMs 300, and workspaceFolders capped at 10 roots with at least one open document.

items.title: Overflow selection algorithm is not locked
items.statement: The contract demands deterministic exclusions but does not specify which eligible roots survive when more than the configured cap contain open documents.
items.impact: Different deterministic orderings can initialize different workspaces and produce different language-server results.
items.builder_discretion: Choose the ordering or priority rule used to retain ten eligible roots.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: workspaceFolders includes only roots with at least one open document up to the configured cap, and deterministic overflow exclusions are visible in logs and evidence when they affect behavior.

items.title: Configuration privacy and secret handling are not stated
items.statement: The core preserves environment and initialization configuration and requires redb persistence, but it does not state whether these fields may contain secrets or what redaction, encryption, access, and evidence rules apply.
items.impact: Potentially sensitive server environment or initialization values may be persisted or surfaced inconsistently.
items.builder_discretion: Unknown; the core provides no security or privacy handling rule for persisted configuration fields.

items.impact: Plan-governance validation can pass without executable evidence that the product behaviors work.

dimension_assessments.summary: Locked defaults, trigger and refresh policy, workspace overflow, edit application, and virtual-document closure are stated.
The prerequisite client, configuration, persistence, and timing-key capabilities are enumerated.
Open documents, completion triggers, edits, roots, configuration fields, logs, and evidence are named as principal inputs or outputs.
Timing, workspace cap, FileSafe routing, and non-executable checklist boundaries are explicit.
Open and changed document triggers are stated, but timeout and failure state transitions are not.
FileSafe controls mutation safety and LSPSupport owns protocol/client constraints.
The owner document and cross-owner SSOT boundary are explicit.
Concrete runtime and GUI consumers are not assigned by the prerequisite unit metadata.
LSPS-074 is explicitly GUI-related and names user-visible surfaces; runtime-only units are classified non-GUI.
Overflow observability and blocked edit reporting are addressed, but timeout recovery is not specified.
FileSafe mutation controls are explicit, but privacy and secret handling for persisted environment and initialization data are not stated.
Prerequisite ordering and downstream effects are not represented in depends_on or unblocks metadata.
Logs/evidence, persistence, FileSafe routing, and the prohibition on executable work provide operational boundaries.
Timing and a ten-root cap are fixed, but the overflow retention ordering remains unspecified.
No compatibility-only notes or persisted-configuration migration behavior are supplied.
Only plan-migration and plan-index validation surfaces are named; runtime oracles are absent.
Client choice, overflow ordering, timeout recovery, migration, consumers, and security handling remain consequential choices or unknowns.
The virtual-document stance is referenced but not restated, alongside unresolved failure, security, migration, and consumer details.
